title: A large subset meeting every large edge in zero or two vertices, found in cubic time
source_title: A logarithmic approximation of linearly ordered colourings

proof_spans.label: the complete author proof of the labelled lemma, retained line for line

standard_prerequisites.name: Linearly ordered colouring
standard_prerequisites.statement: A colouring of the vertices such that in every edge the colour that appears once and is smallest among the colours present is unique.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the hypothesis on the hypergraph.

standard_prerequisites.name: Implied linear system
standard_prerequisites.statement: The colouring conditions translate into a system of linear equations modulo two over the vertex set, and no variable is fixed when the solution space is not contained in a coordinate hyperplane.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the algebraic description the algorithm works with.

standard_prerequisites.name: Basic solution and parametrisation
standard_prerequisites.statement: The solution set is an affine space, so a generic solution is a basic solution plus a combination of basis vectors.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is what makes the randomised choice of coefficients possible.

core_obligations: Describe a randomised algorithm: choose the coefficients of the affine parametrisation independently at random and take the set of vertices whose coordinate vanishes (source lines 160-166).

Show that the resulting set meets every edge of size three in zero or two vertices and has size at least half the vertex set in expectation, using that no variable is fixed to identify, for each vertex, a basis vector witnessing that the vertex can be made to vanish (source lines 161-175).

Derandomise the random choice by the method of conditional expectations, running through the coefficients one at a time, which gives the deterministic algorithm and the stated cubic running time (source lines 176-182).

proof_roadmap.step: Randomised algorithm from the affine parametrisation of the solution space.
Verification of the size and edge conditions in expectation.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 151-156: given a hypergraph of edge sizes two and three that admits a linearly ordered two-colouring and whose implied linear system fixes no variable, there is an algorithm outputting a vertex subset meeting every edge of size three in zero or two vertices, of size at least half the vertices, in time cubic in the number of vertices. The proof (source lines 158-182) does not construct the set directly: it parametrises the solution space of the linear system as an affine space, chooses the coefficients at random, and reads the set off the vanishing coordinates, which requires the hypothesis that no variable is fixed in order to find, for every vertex, a basis direction that can make it vanish; the determinism and the running time are then obtained by derandomisation. The statement records the existence of the algorithm and neither the parametrisation nor the derandomisation.
